messages:
maria: noticing a flurry of GPU pending in eu-west1 this morning, lots of small jobs piling up :thinking_face:
kevin: yep saw that, the fast-provision pool dropped from 120 -> 80 overnight and never recovered
ashley: any errors in the provisioner logs?
maria: probed the reconciler, seeing `heartbeat mismatch` + `lease TTL expired` spam across slots around 06:12 UTC, provisioning requests succeeded but slots never marked Ready
kevin: that sounds like the slot-announcer pod didn't get the lease refresh after a restart — we had a rolling restart of fleet-agent last deploy window
sre-bot: NOTE: Incident detector triggered for provisioner-rate > 0.2 and pending-gpu > 50 in eu-west1
leo: grabbed the logs, snippet: ```
2026-03-23T06:12:03Z reconciler: slot=eu-west1-az1-12 event=lease_refresh err=heartbeat_mismatch expected=162345 got=0
2026-03-23T06:12:04Z slot-manager: mark_pooled_slot_ready failed slot=... reason=ttl_expired
```
maria: apparently the slot heartbeat schema changed in 2.4.1 -> 2.5.0 and the fleet-agent didn't interpret the new field `heartbeat_epoch` so checks failed silently
kevin: oof. did we roll that agent anywhere else?
leo: rolled to eu-west1 yesterday as part of infra-canary, only half the fleet. others still on 2.4.x so mixed-version mismatch is likely root cause
ashley: mitigation idea: bump lease TTL and force reconciler to treat absent `heartbeat_epoch` as legacy 0 for a short window, rollout a fix to 2.5.1 patched image
maria: agreed. temporary workaround applied: `kubectl patch cm gpu-provisioner-config -n infra -p '{"data":{"lease_ttl":"90s"}}'` — increased from 30s to 90s
kevin: did that free up anything?
sre-bot: Autoscaler: noticed pool target increased to 140 after TTL bump, but actual ready slots still 82 (waiting for reconciler sweep)
leo: kicked off a manual sweep job: `./tools/sweep-ready.sh --region eu-west1 --force` to re-evaluate slots and claim orphaned ones
maria: sweep claimed ~26 slots, pending count dropped by 22, but we still have ~15 pods stuck with `AttachVolume` waiting on NVLINK attach handshake failures — probably unrelated but magnifies impact
ashley: long-term fix tracked in #infra: add backward compatibility in heartbeat parser and add a feature-flag for strict-epoch-checking, PR opened (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/provisioner/pull/412)
kevin: what's plan for rollback if 2.5.1 hits weirdness?
leo: canary to 10% in eu-west1a then 30% across region, monitor `slot_ready_latency` and `lease_error_rate`. autopromote disabled. if error_rate > 0.05 revert to 2.4.x image with helm rollback: `helm rollback gpu-provisioner 4`
maria: ops checklist executed: bumped TTL, ran sweep, scaled fast-provision pool +20 to give headroom, opened PR for parser fallback. any cost concerns?
kevin: scaling +20 for 3 hours is ~0.8x hourly spend spike but cheaper than blocked ML pipelines and customer timeouts — ops approved via #finance :heavy_check_mark:
ashley: postmortem TODOs: add migration test for heartbeat schema, add metric `heartbeat_schema_mismatch_total`, and add alert with runbook linking to sweep tool
leo: FYI we also saw a correlated bump in egress retries during the same window, might be an unrelated transient cloud control-plane blip, tracking separately
maria: moving to execute the 2.5.1 canary now, monitoring dashboards updated. will ping when it's stable or we decide to revert :rocket:
kevin: thanks team, keep updates here. if anything blocks customer traffic escalate to oncall and mention @sre-oncall
ashley: ack
leo: will post final summary in #incidents once resolved
